opening.text: What we eat shapes our body. What we watch, read and scroll shapes our mind and spirit. Most of us would think twice about eating junk food at every meal. But we often give our minds that kind of diet without a second thought. Media and technology are good tools. They just need a wise plate.

mainMessage.text: Media and technology can bless us. Wise choices keep them in their place and keep our minds and hearts clean.

blocks.text: **Fill the plate with good things** There is a lot of good to watch, read and learn. Paul told us where to put our thoughts.

Finally, brethren, whatsoever things are true, whatsoever things are honest, whatsoever things are just, whatsoever things are pure, whatsoever things are lovely, whatsoever things are of good report; if there be any virtue, and if there be any praise, think on these things.
Elder Dallin H. Oaks of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Good, Better, Best” from the October 2007 general conference.
Of course it is good to view wholesome entertainment or to obtain interesting information.
The good is real.
**Portions matter** Even good food can be too much. Time is the same. We can't give unlimited hours to one thing.

And see that all these things are done in wisdom and order; for it is not requisite that a man should run faster than he has strength. And again, it is expedient that he should be diligent, that thereby he might win the prize; therefore, all things must be done in order.
Elder Dallin H. Oaks of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Good, Better, Best” from the October 2007 general conference.
But not everything of that sort is worth the portion of our life we give to obtain it.
Watch the portion.
**What comes first** A meal has a main dish. So does life. The Lord told us what to seek first.
But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you.
Elder Dallin H. Oaks of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Good, Better, Best” from the October 2007 general conference.
Surfing the Internet is not better than serving the Lord or strengthening the family.
Put first things first.
**Good is not always enough** A snack can be good and still not be what we need. We can choose better. We can choose best.

Wherefore, I beseech of you, brethren, that ye should search diligently in the light of Christ that ye may know good from evil; and if ye will lay hold upon every good thing, and condemn it not, ye certainly will be a child of Christ.
Elder Dallin H. Oaks of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Good, Better, Best” from the October 2007 general conference.
As we consider various choices, we should remember that it is not enough that something is good.
Reach for the best.
**Guard what goes in** Some things are harmful. We don't need to taste them to know. We can say no early.
Keep thy heart with all diligence; for out of it are the issues of life.
Elder Dallin H. Oaks of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Pornography” from the April 2005 general conference.
Don’t accommodate any degree of temptation.
Guard the heart.
**If we have slipped** Many of us have eaten from the wrong plate. The Savior can clean us and help us start fresh.
If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.
Elder Dallin H. Oaks of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Pornography” from the April 2005 general conference.
Through repentance he can be clean.
He can be clean.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when they set a limit on screens or media and it helped. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Mary chooses the good part

blocks.text: Martha was busy with many things. Her sister Mary sat at the feet of Jesus Christ and listened.

And she had a sister called Mary, which also sat at Jesus’ feet, and heard his word. And Jesus answered and said unto her, Martha, Martha, thou art careful and troubled about many things: But one thing is needful: and Mary hath chosen that good part, which shall not be taken away from her.
Martha wasn't doing wrong things. But Mary chose the best thing. In a busy, loud world, choosing the one thing needful is a good plan.

application.text: First, check how much time you spend on screens this week. Second, trade one hour for something better, like family, service or scripture. Third, put your phone away during meals and prayer.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know God wants me to use my time well. I know good choices lead to a clear mind and a light heart. I know Jesus Christ is the one thing needful. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

invitations: I invite you to check how much time you spend on screens this week.
I invite you to trade one hour for something better, like family, service or scripture.
I invite you to put your phone away during meals and prayer.
blessings: You will have more time for what matters.
You will feel the Spirit more.

closingVerse.text: See then that ye walk circumspectly, not as fools, but as wise, Redeeming the time, because the days are evil.

opening.text: You choose who comes through your front door. You wouldn't let just anyone walk into your living room and talk to your children. Yet every phone, tablet and television is a front door. The question is who we let in, and for how long. Wise people guard the door.

mainMessage.text: Every screen is a front door to our home. A wise family decides who comes in.

blocks.text: **Welcome the good guests** A good home is full of good company. There is plenty of wholesome content to welcome in.

Finally, brethren, whatsoever things are true, whatsoever things are honest, whatsoever things are just, whatsoever things are pure, whatsoever things are lovely, whatsoever things are of good report; if there be any virtue, and if there be any praise, think on these things.
Elder Dallin H. Oaks of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Good, Better, Best” from the October 2007 general conference.
Of course it is good to view wholesome entertainment or to obtain interesting information.
Welcome the good.
**Even good guests can stay too long** A friendly guest who never leaves takes over the house. Time on screens can do the same.

And see that all these things are done in wisdom and order; for it is not requisite that a man should run faster than he has strength. And again, it is expedient that he should be diligent, that thereby he might win the prize; therefore, all things must be done in order.
Elder Dallin H. Oaks of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Good, Better, Best” from the October 2007 general conference.
But not everything of that sort is worth the portion of our life we give to obtain it.
Set a time to go home.
**The home's true purpose** A home exists for family and faith. A screen shouldn't take the place of either.
But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you.
Elder Dallin H. Oaks of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Good, Better, Best” from the October 2007 general conference.
Surfing the Internet is not better than serving the Lord or strengthening the family.
The home comes first.
**Choosing the best company** Good company is nice. Better company lifts us. The best company draws us toward Christ.

Wherefore, I beseech of you, brethren, that ye should search diligently in the light of Christ that ye may know good from evil; and if ye will lay hold upon every good thing, and condemn it not, ye certainly will be a child of Christ.
Elder Dallin H. Oaks of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Good, Better, Best” from the October 2007 general conference.
As we consider various choices, we should remember that it is not enough that something is good.
Choose the best company.
**Lock the door against harm** Some visitors should never come in. A lock on the door is wise, and so are filters, boundaries and open talks in the family.
Keep thy heart with all diligence; for out of it are the issues of life.
Elder Dallin H. Oaks of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Pornography” from the April 2005 general conference.
Don’t accommodate any degree of temptation.
Lock the door.
**If the door was left open** Many of us have let in what we should not have. The Lord helps us clean the house.
If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.
Elder Dallin H. Oaks of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Pornography” from the April 2005 general conference.
Through repentance he can be clean.
The house can be cleaned.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when they closed the door on something harmful. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: David looks from the roof

blocks.text: David was a good king. One evening, he stood on his roof and looked at something he should not have.

And it came to pass in an eveningtide, that David arose from off his bed, and walked upon the roof of the king’s house: and from the roof he saw a woman washing herself; and the woman was very beautiful to look upon.
A look became a thought, and a thought became a choice that hurt many people. David's story warns us how fast things move. It also shows why we turn away early.

application.text: First, set one house rule for screens, like no devices in bedrooms at night. Second, talk about it together. Third, ask each family member to share one good thing they saw online this week.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know a home with good boundaries is a happy home. I know God helps us when we try. I know Jesus Christ stands at the door and knocks. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

invitations: I invite you to set one house rule for screens, like no devices in bedrooms at night.
I invite you to talk about it together.
I invite you to ask each family member to share one good thing they saw online this week.
blessings: Your family will understand and support the rule.
Your family will focus on what is good.

closingVerse.text: And thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children, and shalt talk of them when thou sittest in thine house, and when thou walkest by the way, and when thou liest down, and when thou risest up.

opening.text: A hammer can build a house or break a window. The hammer isn't good or bad. It depends on the hand that holds it. Phones, apps and screens are like that. They can connect a family across the world. They can also steal hours and fill the mind with harm. The choice is in the hand.

mainMessage.text: Media and technology are tools. In wise hands they build. In careless hands they break.

blocks.text: **A tool for good** Builders love their tools. There is a lot of good a screen can do. Wholesome things are worth our time.

Finally, brethren, whatsoever things are true, whatsoever things are honest, whatsoever things are just, whatsoever things are pure, whatsoever things are lovely, whatsoever things are of good report; if there be any virtue, and if there be any praise, think on these things.
Elder Dallin H. Oaks of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Good, Better, Best” from the October 2007 general conference.
Of course it is good to view wholesome entertainment or to obtain interesting information.
A tool for good.
**Don't swing it all day** A builder puts the hammer down when the job is done. We need to do the same with screens.

And see that all these things are done in wisdom and order; for it is not requisite that a man should run faster than he has strength. And again, it is expedient that he should be diligent, that thereby he might win the prize; therefore, all things must be done in order.
Elder Dallin H. Oaks of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Good, Better, Best” from the October 2007 general conference.
But not everything of that sort is worth the portion of our life we give to obtain it.
Put the tool down.
**What we are building** The tool serves the project. Our project is a family and a faith. A tool should never replace the thing we are building.
But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you.
Elder Dallin H. Oaks of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Good, Better, Best” from the October 2007 general conference.
Surfing the Internet is not better than serving the Lord or strengthening the family.
Keep the project first.
**Using the right tool** A good builder picks the right tool for the job. Some tools are good. Others are better for what we are building.

Wherefore, I beseech of you, brethren, that ye should search diligently in the light of Christ that ye may know good from evil; and if ye will lay hold upon every good thing, and condemn it not, ye certainly will be a child of Christ.
Elder Dallin H. Oaks of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Good, Better, Best” from the October 2007 general conference.
As we consider various choices, we should remember that it is not enough that something is good.
Pick the right tool.
**Tools to leave in the shed** Some tools do harm in any hand. A wise builder keeps them away from the job and away from the children.
Keep thy heart with all diligence; for out of it are the issues of life.
Elder Dallin H. Oaks of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Pornography” from the April 2005 general conference.
Don’t accommodate any degree of temptation.
Leave it in the shed.
**Repairing what was damaged** Builders repair things. The Savior repairs people. No damage is too much for Him.
If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.
Elder Dallin H. Oaks of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Pornography” from the April 2005 general conference.
Through repentance he can be clean.
He repairs people.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when they used technology to bless someone. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Alma teaches his son

blocks.text: Alma gave his son Helaman records to guard and sacred counsel to keep. He told him what to do while he was young.
O, remember, my son, and learn wisdom in thy youth; yea, learn in thy youth to keep the commandments of God.
Alma trusted his son with something powerful. He also gave him a clear plan for using it. We can teach our own children the same way, with trust and with a clear plan.

application.text: First, name one way technology helps your family. Second, name one way it gets in the way. Third, make one change that keeps the first and fixes the second.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know good tools bless good lives. I know God helps us choose wisely. I know Jesus Christ is the Master Builder. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

invitations: I invite you to name one way technology helps your family.
I invite you to name one way it gets in the way.
I invite you to make one change that keeps the first and fixes the second.
blessings: You will use technology for good.
You will protect what matters most.

closingVerse.text: But behold, that which is of God inviteth and enticeth to do good continually; wherefore, every thing which inviteth and enticeth to do good, and to love God, and to serve him, is inspired of God.

opening.text: A water filter doesn't make water less enjoyable. It makes it safe to drink. Without one, you can't see what is in the cup. The world gives us a river of media. Some of it is clean. Some is not. A wise person puts a filter in place before drinking.

mainMessage.text: Wise choices act like a filter. They let the good through and keep the harm out.

blocks.text: **Plenty of clean water** A filter isn't about avoiding water. Most of the river is good, and we can drink it.

Finally, brethren, whatsoever things are true, whatsoever things are honest, whatsoever things are just, whatsoever things are pure, whatsoever things are lovely, whatsoever things are of good report; if there be any virtue, and if there be any praise, think on these things.
Elder Dallin H. Oaks of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Good, Better, Best” from the October 2007 general conference.
Of course it is good to view wholesome entertainment or to obtain interesting information.
Most of the river is clean.
**Not too much at once** Even clean water, if gulped without end, drowns. We need measure.

And see that all these things are done in wisdom and order; for it is not requisite that a man should run faster than he has strength. And again, it is expedient that he should be diligent, that thereby he might win the prize; therefore, all things must be done in order.
Elder Dallin H. Oaks of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Good, Better, Best” from the October 2007 general conference.
But not everything of that sort is worth the portion of our life we give to obtain it.
Drink in measure.
**What the water is for** We drink to live, not live to drink. Screens serve life. They aren't life.
But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you.
Elder Dallin H. Oaks of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Good, Better, Best” from the October 2007 general conference.
Surfing the Internet is not better than serving the Lord or strengthening the family.
Screens serve life.
**Filtering for the best** The filter's work is not only to stop poison. It also helps us pick the best source.

Wherefore, I beseech of you, brethren, that ye should search diligently in the light of Christ that ye may know good from evil; and if ye will lay hold upon every good thing, and condemn it not, ye certainly will be a child of Christ.
Elder Dallin H. Oaks of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Good, Better, Best” from the October 2007 general conference.
As we consider various choices, we should remember that it is not enough that something is good.
Choose the best source.
**Keep the poison out** Some water can't be made safe. We don't drink it at all.
Keep thy heart with all diligence; for out of it are the issues of life.
Elder Dallin H. Oaks of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Pornography” from the April 2005 general conference.
Don’t accommodate any degree of temptation.
Don't taste the poison.
**Pure water can be restored** A well that was fouled can be cleaned. Through the Savior, our hearts can be clean again.
If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.
Elder Dallin H. Oaks of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Pornography” from the April 2005 general conference.
Through repentance he can be clean.
The well can be cleaned.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when they chose to turn away from something, and felt peace. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Eve sees the fruit

blocks.text: Eve was in a good place with good things. Then she looked at the one thing she was told not to take.

And when the woman saw that the tree was good for food, and that it was pleasant to the eyes, and a tree to be desired to make one wise, she took of the fruit thereof, and did eat, and gave also unto her husband with her; and he did eat.
Things that look pleasant can still cost us. It helps to decide ahead of time what we will and won't do. And if we fall, the Savior lifts us.

application.text: First, set a filter on your devices, or help your family do so. Second, pick one app or show to cut back on. Third, talk with a friend or family member about what you found.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know God gave us good things to enjoy and a way to keep them safe. I know He forgives and cleans. I know Jesus Christ is the living water. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

invitations: I invite you to set a filter on your devices, or help your family do so.
I invite you to pick one app or show to cut back on.
I invite you to talk with a friend or family member about what you found.
blessings: You will feel more at peace.

closingVerse.text: Ponder the path of thy feet, and let all thy ways be established.

opening.text: On an old radio, you turn the dial. Static, static, then a clear voice. You can't hear every station at once. You choose which one to tune in. Our lives have many stations now. Music, news, videos, messages. The voice of the Spirit is quiet. If we want to hear it, we have to tune the dial.

mainMessage.text: We choose the station. Wise use of media and technology keeps the dial tuned where the Spirit can be heard.

blocks.text: **Good stations exist** There is a lot of clear, good signal out there. We don't have to turn the radio off. We just have to tune it.

Finally, brethren, whatsoever things are true, whatsoever things are honest, whatsoever things are just, whatsoever things are pure, whatsoever things are lovely, whatsoever things are of good report; if there be any virtue, and if there be any praise, think on these things.
Elder Dallin H. Oaks of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Good, Better, Best” from the October 2007 general conference.
Of course it is good to view wholesome entertainment or to obtain interesting information.
Good stations exist.
**Don't leave it on all day** A radio left on all day drowns out the quiet. Our time is limited, and every hour has a price.

And see that all these things are done in wisdom and order; for it is not requisite that a man should run faster than he has strength. And again, it is expedient that he should be diligent, that thereby he might win the prize; therefore, all things must be done in order.
Elder Dallin H. Oaks of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Good, Better, Best” from the October 2007 general conference.
But not everything of that sort is worth the portion of our life we give to obtain it.
Turn it down sometimes.
**The station that matters most** The Lord's voice is the one that matters most. Everything else comes after.
But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you.
Elder Dallin H. Oaks of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Good, Better, Best” from the October 2007 general conference.
Surfing the Internet is not better than serving the Lord or strengthening the family.
Tune to Him first.
**Choosing a clearer signal** Some stations are fine. Some are better. A few are best. A wise listener keeps turning the dial toward clarity.

Wherefore, I beseech of you, brethren, that ye should search diligently in the light of Christ that ye may know good from evil; and if ye will lay hold upon every good thing, and condemn it not, ye certainly will be a child of Christ.
Elder Dallin H. Oaks of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Good, Better, Best” from the October 2007 general conference.
As we consider various choices, we should remember that it is not enough that something is good.
Turn toward clarity.
**Static we can do without** Some signals only bring noise and harm. We don't have to listen to those at all.
Keep thy heart with all diligence; for out of it are the issues of life.
Elder Dallin H. Oaks of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Pornography” from the April 2005 general conference.
Don’t accommodate any degree of temptation.
Turn off the static.
**Finding the signal again** Sometimes we lose the signal. The Savior helps us find it again. Repentance retunes the dial.
If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.
Elder Dallin H. Oaks of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Pornography” from the April 2005 general conference.
Through repentance he can be clean.
The signal returns.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when they turned off the noise and heard the Spirit more clearly. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Jesus goes to a quiet place

blocks.text: The Savior had crowds around Him all day. Still, He made time to be alone with His Father.
And in the morning, rising up a great while before day, he went out, and departed into a solitary place, and there prayed.
Jesus Christ had every reason to stay busy. He went to a quiet place instead. If He needed that time, so do we.

application.text: First, choose a quiet time each day when your phone is off. Second, use it for prayer or scripture. Third, notice what you hear.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know the Spirit speaks in a still, small voice. I know that quiet time makes room for it. I know Jesus Christ is always ready to speak peace to our hearts. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

invitations: I invite you to choose a quiet time each day when your phone is off.
I invite you to use it for prayer or scripture.
I invite you to notice what you hear.
blessings: You will hear the still, small voice.
You will feel closer to God.

closingVerse.text: Yea, thus saith the still small voice, which whispereth through and pierceth all things, and often times it maketh my bones to quake while it maketh manifest, saying:

stories.Story: Jesus goes to a quiet place

sources.verses: Philippians 4:8; Mosiah 4:27; Matthew 6:33; Moroni 7:19; Proverbs 4:23; 1 John 1:9; Luke 10:39, 41–42; 2 Samuel 11:2; Alma 37:35; Genesis 3:6; Mark 1:35.
